quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You must yield to children playing in the street.
questions.explanation: You must drive carefully where children are present. Slow down near schools, playgrounds, and residential areas.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while under the influence of alcohol is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking. It endangers both you and everyone else on the road.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You must change how you drive when weather changes suddenly.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you during bad weather.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you while driving?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and coordination. It makes you feel overly confident and impairs your judgment. Your vision and ability to judge distance also suffer, making it hard to react to danger.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Your brake lights show other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Keep your brake lights in good working order.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal first. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one else is entering that lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Continue driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection go first. You can proceed, but drive at a speed that lets you stop if the light changes.

questions.question: This sign indicates that:

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on an upcoming hill.
There are trucks on an upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill or downgrade is ahead.

questions.question: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride their bikes.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are hard to see at night, even with lights and reflectors. Both drivers and cyclists must be extra alert at night to avoid collisions.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must be followed only when other traffic is present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and help drivers drive safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: Smoking and getting ready to smoke while driving:
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you by taking your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: If you are in a serious crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle off the road if possible. If anyone is injured, call 911. You must report crashes to police if there is an injury, death, or more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: A sign of drunk driving is:

options.text: Driving slower than the normal traffic flow.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving, driving slowly, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: It is illegal to smoke a cigarette:

options.text: If a child is in the vehicle.
While driving in a residential area.
If you are driving at night.
While driving between May and September.

questions.correctAnswerText: If a child is in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: You cannot smoke in a vehicle when carrying a child age 15 or younger. This is against the law.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to them and yell.

questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and keep driving safely to avoid road rage.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure the lane is clear before you move.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers must focus fully on driving. Any extra activity can be a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no warning signals, you should slow down, look, and listen.
questions.explanation: At crossings without warning devices, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains. Only cross when it is safe.

questions.question: What happens if you mix alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps cure a cold.
The effects of both can multiply.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both can multiply.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with medicine can increase how much both affect you. One drink with cold medicine could affect you as much as several drinks alone.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on an interstate?

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Instead, go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: Only vehicles with disability plates or placards can park in spaces marked for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: Parking spaces marked for people with disabilities can only be used by vehicles with disability license plates or disability parking placards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers to be careful. The road may be wet and slippery, which can make it harder to drive safely.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Keeps the seat belt buzzer or light from operating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should rest comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What should you do if a police officer stops you?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the steering wheel. Tell passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.
